addVolumes.doneRecreated: Recreated as {name}; the old container was kept under a new name and can be deleted
addVolumes.startHint: Leave unchecked to keep the original run state (a container that was not running will not be started behind your back).

advanced.capabilityConflict: A capability cannot be both added and dropped

advanced.deviceInvalid: Each line must be host[:container[:perms]] with perms made of r / w / m
advanced.devicesWarning: Mapping a host device into a container hands control of that device to it. Use with care.
advanced.healthDisable: Disable the health check inherited from the image
advanced.healthInvalid: Provide the check command; every interval and count must be at least 1
advanced.logDriverInvalid: Driver options must be key=value per line
advanced.memoryInvalid: Enter a non-negative integer in MiB; at least 6 MiB when non-zero
advanced.sysctlInvalid: Each line must be key=value with a unique key
advanced.ulimitInvalid: Each line must be name or name=soft:hard with a unique name

detail.envHint: ⚠️ Environment values often hold passwords / tokens — do not share screenshots

duplicate.defaultName: Will be created as {name}-copy; a sequence number is appended if the name is taken.

rename.invalid: Name may only contain letters, digits and _ . -, and must start with a letter or digit
rename.label: New name
rename.title: Rename container

update.cpusInvalid: Enter a positive number (decimals allowed), up to 1024 cores
update.cpusPlaceholder: Leave blank to keep unchanged, e.g. 1.5
update.hint: Only the restart policy and resource limits can be updated in place. Image, ports, environment variables, mounts and networks require recreating the container.
update.memoryInvalid: Enter a positive integer of at least 6 MiB (the Docker daemon's hard minimum)
update.noUnlimited: Limits cannot be cleared here: Docker treats 0 in an update as "not specified", so it returns success without applying anything. Removing a limit requires recreating the container.
update.title: Update container settings

delete.soft: Deletion is soft: the name is released and can be registered again.

counts.unavailable: Resource counts are unavailable while the host is offline

host.empty: No hosts registered yet — add the first one.

engine.hint: All of it comes from the daemon’s /version and /info responses — no extra Docker call.
engine.title: Engine info

form.authEditHint: When editing, leaving these empty keeps the stored credentials; switching to \"no auth\" clears them.
form.authHint: TLS and Basic are mutually exclusive; selecting neither means no auth.
form.endpointSocketHint: A local socket endpoint starts with /, e.g. /var/run/docker.sock
form.endpointTcpHint: A remote endpoint starts with tcp:// or https:// and includes a port
form.name: Host name
form.nameHint: The name is the external identifier (the hostId in URLs) and cannot be changed later.

form.testFailed: Cannot connect: check the endpoint, the credentials and whether the target host is reachable.
form.testOk: Connected: this configuration reaches the daemon.
form.tlsNote: These are file paths visible inside the container, not certificate contents; all three are required (a missing CA means accepting any server certificate).

delete.keepHosts: Hosts in this group are not deleted — they simply return to \"ungrouped\".

group.descriptionHint: Leave empty to clear the description.

group.listHint: Groups affect how the overview page is laid out and where selection / filtering boundaries fall, but they play no part in authorization — which hosts someone may touch is decided only by scoped role assignments.
group.name: Group name
group.nameHint: The three built-in groups use English identifiers (production / staging / local) and are shown translated; custom groups appear exactly as you type them.

hero.notFound: Host not found — it may have been removed

info.hint: CPU count and total memory are static limits (the Docker API exposes no host-level live metrics).

empty.title: No repositories yet. Add an address and credentials here before pushing images.

repository.footnote: Passwords are stored AES-GCM encrypted with repository.key in the data volume. Back it up together with the database: either one alone cannot restore.

form.addressHint: Host and optional port only, without http:// or a path; port defaults to 443

error.accountPair: Provide both username and password, or neither (anonymous)

test.anonymousOnly: Reachable, but not authenticated (anonymous access or invalid credentials)
test.unreachable: Unreachable: check network, port and firewall

roleAssign.empty: No hosts yet. Add one from Hosts first.
roleAssign.footnote: Assignment is idempotent: the same (user, role, scope) triple returns the same record. Revocation is a soft delete, so the same triple can be assigned again. Built-in roles have a fixed permission set — create a custom role if you need a different combination.

global.placeholder: Pick global roles (multi-select; leave empty for no global assignment)
global.title: Global scope

roleAssign.globalHint: A global assignment contributes the role's global permissions (user.* / role.* / repository.* / host.manage / audit.read); its host-scoped permissions then apply to every host.
roleAssign.hostHint: Applies on that host only — and the role's global permissions are ignored here. Otherwise "assign admin on one host" would be a silent system-wide promotion.
roleAssign.model: Authorization is a (user, role, scope) triple: one host can hold several roles at once and the effective permissions are their union.
roleAssign.title: Assign roles

action.setDefaultHint: The default role is used when a new user is created without one

confirm.inUse: Role "{name}" still has {count} active assignment(s); the server refuses to delete it (1512) — revoke them first.
confirm.title: Delete role

delete.hint: Built-in roles ship with the system and cannot be deleted

form.name: Role identifier
form.nameHint: 2–32 chars using letters, digits and . _ - only; it travels through tokens and APIs, so it cannot be changed later.
form.nameImmutable: The role identifier cannot be changed: users already reference it.
form.permissionsHint: You may leave this empty — creating a role first and configuring permissions later is a real workflow.

matrix.builtInOnly: Only built-in roles exist right now. Their permission sets are fixed by the migration — create a custom role for a different combination.
matrix.footnote: Ticking a box overwrites that role's permission set; built-in roles are read-only (their set is fixed by the migration).
matrix.title: Permission matrix

status.realtimeHint: Host-level CPU / memory / network are not supported — the Docker API has no such endpoint; container-level metrics live in the container list. Disk usage comes from system/df.
